evidenceFlow.title: Scope
evidenceFlow.detail: All six supplied FIT activities from the Sa Calobra camp week are included. UTC record timestamps are displayed in Europe/Madrid time.

evidenceFlow.title: Integrity
evidenceFlow.detail: Every file passed signature, declared-length, header CRC, file CRC, fitdecode full decode, and an independent Garmin FIT SDK 21.218 integrity check. Across 76,189 records there are no duplicate or backward timestamps.

evidenceFlow.title: Effort method
evidenceFlow.detail: Exact one-second rolling averages preserve recorded zeroes, split at every normalized timer restart and timestamp gap, and reject any window containing missing power. Overlapping qualifying starts are merged into connected effort bouts before counting distinct efforts.

evidenceFlow.title: Known limits
evidenceFlow.detail: 116 power fields are missing (0.152%), all at timer restarts; headline effort windows contain none. Garmin IF, TSS and native power zones are conditional on the 250 W FTP stored in every file. Oct 20 absolute altitude has a barometric offset. FIT data alone cannot identify why heart rate or power changed.

rows.target: 2–3 days off or genuinely easy; delay testing until sleep, soreness, energy and resting HR feel near baseline.
rows.progression: Resume endurance first. A fresh benchmark is usually more informative about 5–7 days after the block than immediately after it.
rows.why: Six consecutive ride days produced 1,066 Garmin TSS; the final three days held 61% of the load.
rows.confidence: High for the need to absorb load; exact recovery time is individual.

rows.target: 2 × 15 min at 235–240 W, then 2 × 20 min; keep rep two within about 3% of rep one.
rows.progression: Once repeatable fresh, place the set after roughly 2 hours of endurance riding.
rows.why: The Queen Stage delivered 241 W for 30 min after 3:04 of riding with only a 3.2% half-to-half fade.
rows.confidence: Conditional on the file-stored 250 W FTP remaining appropriate.

rows.target: Aim for first/second-half power within about 3%; avoid spending the first half above the power you can defend.
rows.progression: Use the Queen Stage effort as the model; review power and HR halves after comparable climbs.
rows.why: The Oct 19 best 20 min faded roughly 12% in power while HR rose; terrain, heat and fueling may also contribute.
rows.confidence: Moderate; this is a pacing flag, not a fatigue diagnosis.

rows.target: First reproduce the previously known 263 W for 20 min; only then consider a 267–270 W stretch or 35–40 min near 240–250 W.
rows.progression: Test fresh and under repeatable conditions. Keep 250 W provisional until a controlled result supports changing it.
rows.why: Camp best was 244 W for 20 min mid-block and mid-ride; applying 95% to it would misuse a non-test effort.
rows.confidence: The 263 W comparison comes from prior work, not from these six files, and may be stale.

rows.target: If 250 W remains valid, try 4 × 4 min at roughly 265–280 W; optionally add 4–6 × 8–10 sec fully recovered sprints.
rows.progression: Judge VO₂ only from a controlled session; this camp did not contain a clean maximal 5 min test.
rows.why: The route best 5 min was 260 W, while the final day still showed 839 W for 5 sec—short-power reserve was present.
rows.confidence: Training range, not a diagnosis of weakness or a fixed prescription.
